title: Cam privacy charter
principle: Aaron's personal information and preferences exist inside Cam for exactly one purpose: to help Aaron. They are never released to any other person, agent, service, distillate or channel. Other people may have their own individual prompts and memory; memory is never shared, transmitted, revealed or used across people. Secrecy of personal information is a moral obligation here, not a configuration default.

owner.label: Aaron
owner.notes: The owner's roots are the pre-existing Cam directories; nothing moved. Owner-only files are chmod 700/600 by the kernel.

guest_layout.profile.json: id, label, created, consent (what this person allowed Cam to keep for them)
guest_layout.prompt.md: this person's own prompt — individual, never merged with anyone else's
guest_layout.swarm/: own lineage (chief spawns under this person's root)
guest_layout.distill/: own counts-only distillate — never written to the owner's vault or mesh

principals.guest_tools_notes: Everything else (vault, mesh, MemoryBear, workspaces, tickets, Needs Attention, loops, calendar sources, connectors inventory, privacy audit) reaches the owner's data or configuration and is not listed for a guest process — tools/list omits them and tools/call refuses them.
isolation: A data directory is sealed to one principal at first touch (.principal). Any script that opens a directory sealed to a different principal refuses.
Guests cannot redirect their roots outside data/principals/<id> via environment overrides; the kernel rejects the override.
Guest processes never read the owner's vault, mesh seed, cline cache, workspaces registry paths, calendar sources, or MemoryBear account.
Guest distillates stay inside the guest root; the nightly loop, the mesh, and the vault only ever see the owner's counts-only distillates.
Nothing in Cam merges, compares, or trains across principals. There is no shared memory tier.
Recommended host hardening: give each additional person their own OS user; Cam's owner data is chmod 700 so that user cannot read it even by accident.

personal_info.label: personal information
personal_info.notes: personal_term = tokens from the owner's local vocabulary file (identity/aaron/local/personal-vocabulary.txt, git-ignored). The list itself is personal and never leaves the machine.

personal_preference.label: personal preference / sensitive context
personal_preference.notes: Preferences ('I prefer', 'my favourite', 'I hate') and health / finance / relationship / location context.

operational.label: counts, statuses, ids, timestamps
operational.notes: The only class allowed into mesh distillates.

outbox_draft.notes: Drafts are read by the principal who approves them. A draft addressed to a third party is redacted by the redactor role before Aaron sees it, unless Aaron's consent record names that recipient.

mesh_distillate.notes: Counts only. The kernel refuses to write a distillate containing personal classes.

mcp_response.notes: The MCP server serves one principal per process; guests see a reduced tool set that cannot reach owner roots.

network.notes: No script in this repo posts personal classes anywhere. MemoryBear is the one sanctioned external memory and is owner-scoped by end_user_id.

consent.notes: Sharing any personal class with a named third party requires an explicit consent entry (recipient, classes, expires) written by Aaron at the CLI (`cam_privacy.py consent grant --aaron`). Agents can read consent, never write it.

privileges.notes: disclose_personal is in privilege_catalog.aaron_only, so no agent can ever hold it; cam_swarm doctor and privacy-check both assert it.

invariants.rule: No personal class in any mesh distillate
One process, one principal; owner roots unreachable from a guest principal
Guest MCP exposes only the guest tool allowlist
Memory is per-person: MemoryBear and the vault are owner-only; guests keep memory in their own root
Owner data directories are chmod 700 and files 600
Ledgers are HMAC-sealed when CAM_LEDGER_HMAC_KEY (or identity/aaron/local/ledger.key) exists; tampering is reported by doctor
Mesh notes are redacted; secrets are refused everywhere
Personal vocabulary, consent records, guest roots and keys are git-ignored; privacy-check fails if any are tracked
Third-party recipients need a consent record; drafts to unknown recipients are redacted

tracked_file_allowlist.notes: privacy-check scans tracked config/docs/scripts for identifiers. Documentation fixtures (RFC 2606 example domains, 555 numbers) and vendor/org contact addresses already public in upstream docs are not personal identifiers.

notes: Aaron's first name is the repository's operator label and appears in code and docs; his surname, contact details, addresses, and anything else identifying never appear in tracked files.
Nothing here weakens the draft-only outbound rule; it adds a second gate (privacy) before the first one (approval).
